description: OFF-BALL: WIDEN WHO MAY START A DIAGONAL RUN. Two re-aims inside match::ai::ActionSelectorDiagonalRun::vf5 (0x143e036e0), on the NEW-RUN branch only - the branch taken when 0x143daa970(match, slot, 0x21) reports the player is not already running the action. The two branches are mutually exclusive: 0x143e03a68 `jmp 0x143e03a7f` skips the new-run loads. (A) CANDIDATE CONE 20 deg -> 25 deg. The candidate must lie within a cone of the ball's travel direction; the game's own continuing-run branch already uses 40 deg (0x143e03a53), so 25 is well inside the shipped range. (B) BALL-DISTANCE LEASH 5.0 -> 6.5. maxDist = min(8 - 3f, C) + 2, f = clamp((depth-5)/9, 0, 1), depth = how far the player is behind the opponent defensive line. WHAT IS DEMONSTRATED. (a) EMULATED. I ran the game's own maxDist arithmetic (slice 0x143e03bfb..0x143e03c57) under Unicorn against the PRISTINE image, sweeping depth with xmm7 = 8.0 and xmm15 = 1.0 (the real loads): depth 0 / 5 / 9.5 / 11 / 12 / 14 / 20 gives C=5.0 -> 7.00 7.00 7.00 7.00 7.00 7.00 7.00 (STOCK: a FLAT 7 m leash at every depth, because 8-3f never drops below 5 so the min() always picks C); C=6.5 -> 8.50 8.50 8.50 8.00 7.67 7.00 7.00; C=8.0 -> 10.00 10.00 8.50 8.00 7.67 7.00 7.00. C=12.0 produced a byte-identical curve to C=8.0, so any C >= 8 is equivalent to 8.0 (cell 0x145b52fbc) - there is no point going above it, and C=8 simply makes a new run start from the same distance the game already lets a run in progress be at. (b) DISASSEMBLY, register provenance traced across the whole function. xmm14 is written only at 0x143e03a53 / 0x143e03a6a and read only at 0x143e03d08 (`comiss xmm0, xmm14; ja reject`), so raising it only widens. xmm10 is written only at 0x143e03a5c / 0x143e03a76 and read only at 0x143e03c4a (`minss xmm7, xmm10`), then reloaded with FLT_EPSILON at 0x143e03cbd, so nothing leaks. I also confirmed that every jump out of the region between the two gates lands on the reject label 0x143e03fba (`xorps xmm0, xmm0` = score 0), so the leash and the cone are conjunctive with everything else. (c) INFERRED: game units (metres / degrees, from surrounding geometry) and behaviour under real match state. WHAT CHANGES IN A MATCH - READ THIS BEFORE EXPECTING TOO MUCH OF (B). The selector's success return is `movaps xmm0, xmm9` at 0x143e03fb4, and xmm9 is written exactly once, at 0x143e03a0d: xmm9 = ([rdx + 5*opp*4 + 0x44] - player.x) * dir = the DEPTH BEHIND THE OPPONENT DEFENSIVE LINE. The score IS the depth, so the deepest eligible candidate wins the one diagonal slot. The emulation above shows C=6.5 only lifts maxDist above the stock 7.0 for players shallower than 14 m (depth 13.0 -> 7.33, 13.9 -> 7.03, 14.0 -> 7.00), so anyone admitted ONLY by (B) scores under 14 and loses the slot to any deeper candidate who was already eligible. (B)'s real value is therefore AVAILABILITY, not runner choice: it lets a diagonal run happen at all in the situations where the flat 7 m leash excluded everyone. It changes WHO runs only when no deeper candidate was eligible. (A) is depth-neutral and does not have this problem - it widens the pool at every depth. Neither edit changes how MANY can run at once; that is the maxSlots byte in offball-run-variety.json. WHO: the attacking side only, both teams equally. 0x143d03493 is the ONLY call to the selector-manager update 0x143d52470 in the whole image (byte scan of .xcode and .text for E8/E9 rel32), guarded by `mov ecx,[match+0x3318]; and ecx,1; cmp ecx,[teamAI+8]; jne skip` - one team per frame, selected by that bit (read as the side in possession; that reading is inferred). No human/CPU test exists on the path, so this changes the human's AI team-mates exactly as much as the CPU. Whether the stick-controlled player is excluded is NOT established. BYTES: both instructions are byte-identical in the installed exe and the PRISTINE image; both re-aims keep the same instruction length and operand form; NO pool cell is written (0x145a8dd78 alone has over a thousand referrers and must never be edited in place). Destination cells: 0x145da7de0 = 25.0 (.tls$, 659 refs, writers 0) and 0x146b1ff34 = 6.5 (.tls$, 60 refs, writers 0) - the latter is the only plain f32 6.5 cell in the census; it sits 20 bytes after a lea-referenced pointer block, but the section is non-writable and this patch only reads it. Revert: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/offball-diagonal-band.json

patches.name: A: new-run candidate cone 20 deg -> 25 deg (re-aim 0x145a8aa44 -> 0x145da7de0)
